prompt:
A night city skyline in soft, steady rain, seen across a wide black river: "Rain on the River". Original, generic architecture only — no recognisable real-world landmark or skyline.

Composition: the waterline sits at roughly 58–62% of the height. Above it, 3 depth layers of building silhouettes: far towers pale blue-grey and hazy in the rain, mid towers darker with more detail, near waterfront blocks darkest. Thousands of tiny window lights, mostly warm (amber, soft white) with some cool (teal, pale blue) floors, arranged in believable grids per building, many windows dark; every few seconds one or two windows somewhere slowly fade on or off (people coming home) — very subtle. A few slim spires with slow, soft red aviation lights that fade in and out (2–3 s period, gentle, not strobing). Low clouds hang over the city, lit from below by the city glow in a faint orange-violet; a thin mist band hugs the river.

Water: the river reflects the city as long, broken, vertical light streaks (each lit window cluster becomes a shimmering column), wobbling and breaking up with slow ripples; darker towards the viewer. Occasional rain-drop rings appear and expand on the near water.

Rain: fine, slightly diagonal rain streaks in 2–3 depth layers (far: very faint and thin, near: a little longer and brighter), falling steadily; the rain must never become a bright full-screen flicker. Keep the top-centre clock area calm and dark (night sky and low cloud there, no bright towers directly under the clock).

Layout: build the skyline from lp.w so a 32:9 ultra-wide gets a long, varied skyline (clusters of tall towers, gaps, a bridge with a row of lights spanning part of the river) rather than a stretched 16:10 picture; 5:4 must still be composed; the 320x200 thumbnail must read as "city at night in rain".

Craft: pre-render the sky, clouds, buildings and their windows into layers in resize(); per frame only blend in the few windows that change, the reflections (pre-rendered columns distorted with a few cheap drawImage slices), and the rain (a few pre-rendered rain tiles scrolled at different speeds — not thousands of individual strokes). No shadowBlur or ctx.filter. Pure function of lp.t, phases wrapped for long runs. Aim for ≤ 2.5 ms at 1512x982@2 and < 150 mW in the battery profile. Look at every still (32:9, 16:10, 5:4, thumbnail, t=600) like an art director and refine until it is genuinely beautiful.

prompt:
Art-director notes — a good start (the low cloud glow, the bridge and the rain work well). Refine it to excellent; keep the darkness, the calm clock area and the cost.

1. Depth and haze: the farthest tower layer is the LIGHTEST, flat lavender-grey, so the skyline looks pasted on. Reverse the logic: far towers are dark, desaturated blue-grey silhouettes softened by rain haze (lower contrast, lit windows smaller and dimmer); the haze is brightest just above the waterline (city glow + mist) and fades into the dark cloud ceiling. Add a subtle vertical gradient inside each tower (slightly lighter near the base from the city glow, darker at the top) so they don't look like flat paper cut-outs.
2. Architecture: many towers share the same rectangular window grid. Vary it: some towers with horizontal light bands (lit office floors), some with sparse warm apartment windows, a few glass towers with faint vertical mullion lines, set-back tops, slanted or stepped crowns, a couple of antenna masts. Near waterfront blocks are plain black boxes — give them a few lit ground-floor shop fronts, a warm streetlight row along the embankment and some variety in height.
3. Reflections: the water currently shows a regular grid of short vertical dashes (a barcode pattern). Real reflections at night are long, soft, vertical light columns under each bright cluster, brightest and most continuous near the shoreline, broken by horizontal ripple bands that slowly shift, and fading/stretching towards the viewer. Build them by drawing the city lights layer mirrored, stretched vertically and blurred (draw it into a small offscreen canvas and scale it up), then slice it into horizontal strips offset by a slow sine for the wobble. The bridge lights and the red aviation lights should also reflect.
4. Keep the rain as is, but add a faint, slow mist band drifting along the far shore.

Check all JPEG previews in scene/.check/previews/ (32:9, 16:10, 5:4, thumbnail, t=600) before you finish.

prompt:
Art-director brief — MORE LIFE BEYOND THE RAIN. This scene already passes the motion check — but only because the rain moves everywhere. Underneath it, the city is a still picture: the skyline, the bridge, most windows and the sky barely change. Make the city itself gently, clearly alive, like Apple's live wallpapers: subtle and calm, never busy. Keep what is good — the composition, the towers, the soft steady rain, the long wavering reflections, the palette, and the dark, calm clock region at top centre. Don't redesign; bring the city to life.

1. Sky: low clouds and rain haze drifting slowly across and in front of the skyline in 2–3 layers at different speeds (far 1–3 CSS px/s, near 4–10 on a 1512-px-wide screen), thinning and thickening over 20–60 s so towers fade in and out of the mist; the city glow on the cloud base breathing softly.
2. City life: a few windows switch on or off now and then (eased over ~1 s, a handful per minute across the skyline, never blinking), slow red aviation lights pulsing smoothly, and a faint beacon or rooftop light sweeping slowly on one tower.
3. Traffic on the bridge: tiny warm headlights and red tail lights gliding across the lit bridge in both directions at a believable, slow speed (crossing in ~20–40 s), reflected faintly in the river.
4. The river: a slow boat or barge with a couple of lights crossing every minute or two (ease in/out at the edges), its wake gently disturbing the reflections; rain rings appearing and spreading on the near water; the reflection columns shimmering a little more.
5. Optional: a very slow camera drift of a few % over 1–2 minutes (parallax between far, mid and near towers).

Calm rules: nothing large moves fast, no flashes or strobing, no per-frame randomness, the rain stays soft (don't make it heavier). Behind the clock keep motion dark and low-contrast. Budgets: stay ≤ 3 ms per frame at 1512x982@2 (now 2.0–2.5 ms) and within the 5120x1440 budget; battery-profile energy under 150 mW (now ~56 mW; check with `livepaper live scene`); motion: keep it in all 9 regions with busy and flicker near 0. Look at every still (32:9, 16:10, 5:4, thumbnail, t = 600) like an art director, and also compare stills a few seconds apart (e.g. `livepaper still scene --t 30` and `--t 33`) to judge that the city — not only the rain — changes: it must still be genuinely beautiful. Update the description in scene.json to mention the new motion.
